The best two pieces of advise that I was given when I started playing HOI3:

1) Pick a tech specialization plan and stick to it: That is, decide on a handful of the military techs you want to master and, for all intents and purposes, ignore anything that doesn't support that plan. For GER, for example, pick one tank size and drill down into that tech and stay on-top-of/slightly-ahead-of the curve. Pick only a couple of ships to focus on, and skip the others. You don't need to have fully built out battleship and battlecruiser techlines. Carry this into your production plans: if you want to go with a high-tech infantry, ask yourself why you're bothering to build any militia units - that kind of thing. This will in many ways dictate how you will be fighting your war(s), so pick the tech that will support your plan and vice-versa.

2) Organize, Organize, Organize! - Most of the bigger nations (and GER is no exception) start with some very questionable set-ups in their order of battle. Day 1, Hour 1 of your campaign should be a solid reorganization of the military. Disbanding units that aren't going to support your style of warfare and getting the right units under the right leaders and in the right theaters. Play as the U.S. some time, that's a good hour or two of work right there. :)

Note sure I can offer much in the way of specific German advise, so I'll refine from suggesting much in that regard. One thing I found helpful in almost all of the Paradox games was to start with a "lesser" power in a minor theater (Brazil being one of my favorites). Why deal with the headache of learning new game rules, UI, etc and having to deal with dozens and dozens of unit stacks. Pop over to Brazil and learn with only a handful of units and much more relaxed problems. Worst case scenario: You take over all of South America. :)

I would start building only ships, planes and special forces until around late 37, 38, start pumping out inf when you have the right tech so it doesn't need updates before '40. That saves u a lot of IC to put into other stuff. Keep the light tanks, but don't upgrade them, just build medium tanks when you have the tech and phase the light ones out.

Keep your tanks in designated armor corps, where you have tank commanders at every level of the structure. Build at least 2 corps for pincer movements. 1-2 tank divisions + 2 - 3 mech/motorised to secure the breakthrough make a good corps. I do well with 1 reg tank + 2 reg inf + 1-2 reg mobile arty. These corps are your most important weapon, especially against France.

12 -15 fighter sq when the war starts are usually enough, but keep building them, GB is a pain in the ass. TAC/CAS isz optional vs the AI, you don'T need it, CAS is nice and in Europe useful, but Europe is weak and the only strong enemy is Russia and there they are mostly useless because of the missing airfields.

Marine patrol aircraft are great vs. GB fleet, especially working together wirh your surface fleet. until around '41 Germany has the edge on sea when its in range of it's own marine bombers. You can beat the british fleet to a degree that you can invade it in the summer of 1940. Paratroopers are key. If you don't take GB, you need a lot of fighters to keep GB in check after US joins the war.

You can secure the Maginot-Line with 2-1 divsions per province + some mobile reserves in the back in case FR atttacks. If you add the guards on the eastern border you need around 60 - 80 inf divsions + tanks + mot. inf in 1940 to be on the safe side.

you can do both, just make sure you have a transport fleet of 9 - 12 TP vessels ready + 1 - 2 divisons of paratroopers and the British fleet down to a shadow of her former self in the summer of 1940. But that means you have to fight the Royal Navy from day one. Lure their fleet with your fleet and as soon as they are engaged send your naval bombers and fighters, when you see you might loose a ship: disengage and repair and most of all: don't fight carriers without air cover. When you do that and with a bit of luck, you can land in 1940. Beating GB on the ground is a cakewalk in 1940, the hard part is landing. So it's possible to beat FR and GB in 1940 and still be ready in 1941 for the red menace. But thats tough for a beginner, cause you need to keep an eye for your navy all the time, because as Britain you can afford to loose ships, as Germany not so much.

Good luck and have fun.
